summary: We developed an interactive educational project, "Through the Solar System," featuring a digital game, explanatory video, and research presentation that compares extreme space environments on the Moon and Mars with Earth analogs like Antarctica and the Sahara Desert. Using real NASA temperature data, the project addresses the challenge of selecting safe locations and designing habitable bases in extreme thermal and lighting conditions by proposing solutions such as advanced thermal insulation and reliable heating systems. This work is important because it prepares future scientists to solve off-world survival challenges while supporting Sustainable Development Goals 9, 13, and 17 to advance infrastructure innovation, climate action, and global collaboration.
details: Our project focuses on identifying places on Earth that are similar to the environments of the Moon and Mars. We compare the extreme cold temperatures of Antarctica with the Moon’s South Pole, and the hot, dry conditions of the Sahara Desert with the environment of Mars. The project works by studying and comparing environmental conditions such as temperature, climate, and living challenges. These comparisons help scientists understand the difficulties of building permanent bases on the Moon and Mars. The main benefits are helping scientists prepare for future space exploration, choose suitable locations, and develop solutions for extreme environmental conditions. Our intended impact is to support future human exploration and make living on the Moon and Mars safer and more sustainable. We used NASA research, scientific information, Canva, and presentation tools to develop our project. No special hardware or coding languages were required. Our project is creative because it connects real places on Earth with environments beyond our planet. Our team considered temperature differences, environmental conditions, human safety, and the challenges of long-term living.
